chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the People of the Book and all those who have a covenant (dhimmah), if one of the spouses converts to Islam, they remain upon their marriage, and he is not permitted to take her out of the land of Islam to another land, nor sleep with her, but he visits her during the day. As for the polytheists, they are like the polytheists of the Arabs and others; they remain upon their marriage until the expiration of the waiting period (iddah). If the woman converts and then the man converts before the expiration of her waiting period, she is his wife. If he does not convert except after the expiration of her waiting period, then she is divorced from him and there is no claim for him upon her. And likewise all those who have no covenant. And it is not fitting for a Muslim to marry a Jewish woman or a Christian woman while he finds a free woman or a slave woman.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the marriage of a Muslim and a non-Muslim spouse if one converts to Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of 'keeping the marriage' (al-baqa') for Ahl al-Kitab and polytheists upon one spouse's conversion, distinguishing between those with a covenant (dhimmi) and those without. It establishes that the non-converting spouse retains marital rights during the waiting period (iddah), but if the second spouse converts after the iddah concludes, the bond is permanently severed. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that Islam is the primary barrier to marriage for men, while also noting the preference for marrying free Muslim women over Jewish or Christian ones.
